title: Matic (Disrupt SF 2017 final)

transcript.text: What is the biggest, most emotional purchase that you will likely ever make? It's your home. It's where you'll spend 30 years making memories, and you'll spend 30 years trying to pay it off. And you need to protect this significant purchase with homeowners insurance. But you're not an expert in homeowners insurance. You don't know what the difference is between the insurance carriers are, or what coverages you need, or what's a fair price for you to pay.

And worse, the process is tedious, inefficient, and confusing. It needlessly takes days. I'm here to introduce Matic. Matic makes buying homeowners insurance a breeze. Two to three minutes, and you're done. And homeowners insurance is the requirement on your home loan. And there are two problems getting it. Number one, you have to go to insurance carrier after insurance carrier, filling out your information over and over again. And each carrier is going to ask you 40 to 50 home-specific questions like, what's your roof made out of?

Or do you have a circuit breaker or a fuse box? And how should you know you don't live in the house yet? And the second problem is, unless you're a licensed insurance agent, you don't know what the best policy is for you and your home. And that's why we created Matic. You think Amazon's one click buy it now button, but for homeowners insurance. Matic's API integrates directly with mortgage lenders and insurance carriers to provide homeowners insurance during the mortgage process.

Within 60 seconds or less, Matic will figure out what coverages you need, shop multiple insurance carriers, and give you a quote custom specific to you, and all you have to do is click one button. And let me show you how easy it is. The mortgage process is extremely complicated, and that's why lenders are moving to digital platforms like you see here. Academy is one of the largest lenders in the nation, and they built this portal to help their home buyers get into their house quicker.

And almost every part of this home buying process can be done online, except for homeowners insurance until Matic. Vlad is getting his loan from Academy and now it's time for him to get insurance. He opens his to-do task, simply clicks get quote and his process begins. Now notice that Vlad didn't have to put in his name, his date of birth, his marital status. He doesn't have to know what his roof was made out of or whether it was a circuit breaker or a fuse box.

Vlad didn't have to put in any information at all. Academy sends us his data, VAPI. Matic normalizes the data, adds new layers of data like public record sources, and then passes it to multiple insurance carriers. Now Vlad has to sit back, wait and get his quotes and already, boom, here it is. Matic figured out what coverages are best for Vlad in his home, normalized it against multiple carriers, and then picked the best price for that coverage.

We shop for Vlad in seconds and we explain what he needs and why. Have more questions? Our very own Matic agent will call, email, or text Vlad to review his coverages with him because after all, insurance can be complicated and Matic makes it simple. But not all lenders build their own mortgage platforms. In fact, most don't. For example, JPMorgan Chase uses Rustify, one of the largest and most advanced mortgage platforms out there.

Watch how easy it is for any lender who uses Rustify to use Matic. The lender simply flips a switch in their back end. And now any lender who uses Rustify automatically has Matic's one-click HUI to do. So again here, a simple click get quote, and then the process begins. So why hasn't this been done before? Well, there are many reasons for this, but only now are mortgages going digital.

Two years ago, there was no such thing as a digital mortgage, and now 60% are being done online and growing every day. And for the first time, lenders have the ability to pass as personal and property data via API. And for the first time, insurance carriers have the ability to quote based off this data. And you can't have a digital mortgage without digital insurance, and carriers will pay us for this.

On average, Matic makes $150 per policy per year. This means that every year a customer renews, Matic continues to make $150. The average lifetime value of a customer is five years, which means we'll make $750 over the life of a customer. And because we can't pay lenders due to mortgage regulations, our typical acquisition cost is zero. And better yet, these numbers don't include bundling auto as well.

Around 30% of our customers ask to bundle their auto policy, which doubles or triples our revenue, since we get a reoccurring commission on our auto premium as well. And so by integrating directly with mortgage lenders and piggybacking off the distribution of mortgage platforms like Roostify, Matic's vision is to help home buyers get a policy, a Matic policy, on every loan. And we're one step closer to that vision.

I'm so excited to announce here at Battlefield that we're partnered with Roostify and Mortgage Hippo to great mortgage platforms and lenders like Academy, Mr. Cooper, Freedom, and United Wholesale Mortgage. These are some of the largest names in lending that account for 100 billion with a B in a mortgage originations. brief.headline: Dig deeper: the whole pitch rests on a direct lender and carrier API integration that is unverified, and the one claim we could check, that 60% of mortgages are online, was contradicted.
brief.summary: Matic says its API plugs into mortgage lenders and carriers so a homebuyer can get a homeowners policy in 2-3 minutes with no data entry, at about $150 per policy per year, $750 lifetime value, and zero acquisition cost. The $750 figure is consistent with $150 over 5 years, and Roostify's use by JPMorgan Chase checks out. The integration claim and the prefill claims that depend on it are still unverified. The 60% online-mortgage figure is contradicted, since J.D. Power puts it near 43% for 2017. The 40-50 carrier questions figure has no independent source, and Matic's own site now describes a short form. Live drift also leaves open which lenders are live (one named lender became four) and whether the auto-bundling uplift applies per customer or across the book.
strengths: Clear wedge: insurance bought inside the digital mortgage flow, with distribution through platforms like Roostify (a platform used by JPMorgan Chase and reportedly about 200 lenders) rather than paid acquisition
Simple unit economics that add up: $150 per year x 5 years = $750, with carriers paying and, per the founder, zero acquisition cost
Possible upside from auto bundling: about 30% of customers reportedly ask for it, and it is excluded from the $750
Named lender and platform partners (Academy, Mr. Cooper, Freedom, United Wholesale Mortgage, Roostify, Mortgage Hippo) give specific things to verify

red_flags.text: Everything rests on the claim that Matic's API integrates directly with lenders and carriers. Prefill, auto-populated roof and electrical data, the 2-3 minute purchase, and carriers paying are all downstream of it. None of it is verified, and no live carrier, bound-policy count or production data feed was given.

The 60% online-mortgage market claim is contradicted: J.D. Power says about 43% applied online in 2017. Only looser survey definitions (56% for 2018) come close. This overstates the tailwind and weakens the 'only now possible' argument.

The problem sizing is unsupported: no source gives 40-50 home-specific questions per carrier, and Matic's own site now describes a short form. The share of questions actually prefilled is unknown. The founder first said no name, date of birth or marital status was needed, then said no information at all.

Traction and partner status are unclear. Only Academy was named as a customer in the demo, then three more lenders and two platforms were named at the end. It is unknown which are live and selling policies versus merely reachable. The claim that Roostify lenders get Matic automatically after one switch is unverified. The $100B in originations covers named partners, not Matic volume.

The unit economics and bundling uplift are unverified and inconsistent. The $150 per policy, 5-year life and 30% auto attach rate are unsupported. 'Doubles or triples revenue' implies $300-450 per year per bundled customer, which conflicts with the $750 lifetime value unless it applies per bundled customer.

questions: Which carriers are live and binding policies through the API today, which lender data feeds are in production, and how many policies have actually closed this way?
Which of the named lenders and platforms (Academy, Mr. Cooper, Freedom, United Wholesale Mortgage, Roostify, Mortgage Hippo) are live and selling Matic policies today versus signed or just reachable?
What share of carrier questions do you actually prefill, and what share of users still answer something by hand? Where does 40-50 come from, given your site now says a short form?
Where do $150 per policy per year, a 5-year customer life and a 30% auto attach rate come from, and is the 2-3x revenue uplift per bundled customer or across the whole book?
Which source gives 60% of mortgages online, and how many lenders sit on Roostify or similar platforms and could be reached through the integration?
evidence_requests: List of live carrier and lender integrations with go-live dates, plus API documentation or integration contracts
Bound-policy count by carrier and by channel for the last 6 months, with commission statements showing revenue per policy
Roostify and Mortgage Hippo partnership agreements showing how Matic is distributed, plus a list of lenders live versus contracted with application volumes
Field-level prefill rate by question and carrier, median completion time and drop-off funnel data
Renewal and retention data supporting the 5-year lifetime, and auto commission per policy with attach-rate data
live_notes: Speed claim shifted: first 'two to three minutes, and you're done', later 'within 60 seconds or less' for a quote. This is likely quote vs full purchase, but it should be confirmed.
Data-entry claim escalated from no name, date of birth or marital status to 'didn't have to put in any information at all'.
Customer list grew mid-pitch: Academy was the only lender named in the demo, then Mr. Cooper, Freedom and United Wholesale Mortgage were added at the end, with no live-versus-signed status.
New claims said only live: Mortgage Hippo partnership, $100B in originations across named partners, 30% auto-bundle attach rate, and zero acquisition cost because regulations bar paying lenders.
Auto bundling 'doubles or triples revenue' implies $300-450 per year per bundled customer, versus the stated $150 per year and $750 lifetime value.
The transcript ends mid-question from the judges, so Q&A answers are not captured.

outcome: Finalist, did not win TechCrunch Disrupt SF 2017 Startup Battlefield
